histories.H0: Never advanced beyond generation g3; repository-visible authority is g3.
histories.H1: Advanced to g4 and authorized/emitted a g4 effect, then every repository-visible authority, marker, ref and role-local witness inside the same rollback domain is restored to the exact H0 image at g3.

tested_scope.determinism: The publication decision is a deterministic function only of the surviving observation named for each protocol variant.
tested_scope.availability_requirement: Accept current g3 publication in H0.
tested_scope.safety_requirement: Reject stale g3 publication in H1 after a real g4 authorization/effect occurred.
variants: content-addressed effect naming derived from current g3 content
append-only evidence that is nevertheless inside the same rollback domain
rollback-independent high-watermark witness as an explicit scope-limited escape hatch

observation: For H0 and H1, every tested in-domain repository-only observation is byte-for-byte identical by construction. Therefore every deterministic repository-only protocol takes the same action in both histories. The exhaustive action set has only two cases: accept preserves H0 availability but accepts stale g3 in H1; reject preserves H1 safety but falsely excludes valid g3 in H0.
inference: Within this exact co-rollback model, no deterministic protocol whose entire freshness/claim authority co-rolls back to the H0 image can simultaneously guarantee H0 availability and H1 stale-generation safety. Content-addressed effect IDs do not alter the freshness observation when derived only from rolled-back g3 content. An append-only log that shares the rollback domain also does not alter the observation. A surviving rollback-independent high-watermark can distinguish the histories, but if its value changes the accept/reject decision then it is functionally part of the freshness authority; calling it non-authoritative does not preserve the repository-only premise.
scope_guard: This is a narrow finite indistinguishability result for deterministic decisions under exact co-rollback of all in-domain freshness evidence. It does not rule out randomized availability tradeoffs, hardware/external monotonic state, an external sink that itself enforces a non-rollback floor, or a repository feature proven to survive the modeled rollback domain. Those are separate unresolved candidate classes and must independently satisfy CLEAN, zero-finite-quota, zero-cost and no-protected/manual constraints.

phase1_result.new_falsification: Repository-only recovery cannot infer a past g4 from an exact g3 image after all freshness evidence in the same rollback domain is restored to that image; availability in H0 and stale-generation safety in H1 are mutually incompatible for deterministic repository-only decisions.
phase1_result.minimal_unresolved_child: Find a role-permitted Chat-native monotonic witness or sink-enforced generation floor that provably survives the repository rollback domain, is consulted atomically enough to fence stale publication, requires no protected/admin/manual setup, no richer-mode execution, no finite monthly/trial/paid quota, and zero incremental monetary cost.

conflict_check: One bounded role-local finite-model leaf only; no other worker/O/downstream/legacy semantic input read, no shared ledger read, no scheduler mutation, and no authoritative external effect performed.
continuation: Part104: execute exactly one bounded public-source/connector-capability leaf on whether an otherwise role-permitted GitHub-native object can provide a rollback-independent monotonic witness after force-rewind/delete-recreate without protected/admin/manual setup. Prioritize unreachable commit/object retention and exact documented garbage-collection/reachability guarantees; test whether surviving object existence is guaranteed, freshness-ordered, and usable to atomically fence {generation floor, effect_id}. If no such guarantee exists, persist the narrow blocker and next alternative witness class; do not generalize beyond the documented surface.
